questions.q: A sector of a circle of radius 36 cm has area 54pi cm^2. What is the length of its corresponding arc?
questions.explanation: Using sector area = (theta/360)pi r^2, we get (theta/360)pi(36)^2 = 54pi. This gives theta = 15 degrees. The arc length is then (15/360) x 2pi x 36 = 3pi cm.

questions.q: A 20 cm wire is bent into an arc that subtends 60 degrees at the centre. Taking pi = 22/7, what is the circle radius?
questions.explanation: The wire length is the arc length, so 20 = (60/360) x 2pi r = pi r/3. Hence r = 60/pi. Using pi = 22/7 gives r = 60 x 7/22 = 210/11 cm.

questions.q: Two sectors have radii 7 cm and 21 cm with central angles 120 degrees and 40 degrees respectively. Which comparison is correct?
options: A) Their areas are equal and their arc lengths are in ratio 1:3
B) Their areas are in ratio 3:1 and their arc lengths are equal
C) Their areas are in ratio 1:3 and their arc lengths are equal
D) Both area and arc-length ratios are 1:3
questions.answer: C) Their areas are in ratio 1:3 and their arc lengths are equal
questions.explanation: The first area is (120/360)pi(7^2) = 49pi/3, while the second is (40/360)pi(21^2) = 49pi. Thus the area ratio is 1:3. Their arc lengths are (120/360)2pi(7) and (40/360)2pi(21), both equal to 14pi/3.

questions.q: What is the area of the minor segment of a circle of radius 14 cm subtended by a 60 degree central angle?
questions.explanation: The sector area is (60/360)pi(14^2) = 98pi/3. The triangle formed by the two radii and the chord has two sides 14 with included angle 60 degrees, so it is equilateral and its area is 49sqrt(3). The minor segment area is sector area minus triangle area, giving 98pi/3 - 49sqrt(3) cm^2.
